answer: In an agent economy, one concrete anti-sybil mechanism is compute-attestation bonding: every agent must perform verifiable inference and stake tokens proportional to its scope. Like a scribe with a quill inscribing records, each agent cryptographically signs outputs, creating an immutable trail. Staked capital acts like a rare opal—costly to replicate across thousands of fake identities. When a malicious operator spawns a bot army, aggregate bonding drives their capital to nadir, locking up funds slashed upon misbehavior. Linear cost scaling destroys economies of scale behind sybil attacks.
